generatedCommentsNodes.comment: The schema-parsing logic was changed from `indexOf(':')` (split on the *first* colon only) to `split(":")` (split on *every* colon, taking `header[1]` as the type). For all current ESQL type names this is equivalent, but it is a narrower contract: if a type name ever contained a colon, the old code would preserve it in `typeName` while the new code would truncate it to the segment between the first and second colon. Using `split(":", 2)` would preserve the original "split-on-first-colon" semantics at no cost and make the intent explicit.

In `readMappingFile`, when a key from `typeMapping` is not found in the mapping's `properties` node, it is silently ignored (the `if (propertiesNode.has(key))` guard simply skips it). Since this is test infrastructure, a typo in a type-mapping key (e.g., `"clinet_ip"` instead of `"client_ip"`) would be silently dropped, and the test would run against the unmodified mapping — likely producing a confusing failure far from the root cause. Consider logging a warning or throwing an `IllegalArgumentException` when a type-mapping key is absent from the mapping, so misconfigurations surface immediately.

Uhh, how did that field _not_ end up being widened in the first place? In `Analyzer.mappingAsAttributes`, line 240, each field attribute's field should already have been widened, including the contained `EsField`'s type.

What fails if we do not widen here? I'd like to figure out if this is really necessary.

Also, to avoid confusion in the future, do you think we should add an assert to `FieldAttribute`'s constructor to ensure it only ever gets built with already widened data types?

I was surprised this failed too. It fails later in planning, I don't remember the exact stack trace, but the error was that this function was being called with an unsupported type (the narrow type). I understood the `evaluator` function to be called much later, so I was surprised by this too. I could re-investigate because perhaps there is a code path to this that is happening unnecessarily early?

I think this deserves a follow up, because there begin to be many places were widening is necessary - and we only find out by failed queries/tests :/ I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/112691.

I investigated, and this exception is thrown down during query execution (ie. after local physical planning) during the setup of the type converting block loader at https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/x-pack/plugin/esql/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/esql/planner/EsPhysicalOperationProviders.java#L384.

This is well past any analyzing, planning phases, so it is clear that the types are not widened in general, but only in specific cases. A followup investigation makes a lot of sense.
